pull.title: rpc: return error when invalidateblock fails

<!--
Bitcoin Core has a thorough review process and even the most trivial change
needs to pass a lot of eyes and requires non-zero or even substantial time
effort to review. There is a huge lack of active reviewers on the project, so
patches often sit for a long time.
-->

`invalidateblock` returns `null` even when the block was not invalidated because the RPC does not pay attention to `Chainstate::InvalidateBlock()` return value. If there is a problem disconnecting the block (for example, the undo data is corrupt), the chain remains partially rolled back when telling the user that the operation succeeded. This creates an error in every failure case, including the genesis block case, and makes RPC look at the return value. The error reports a failed block and how far the chain was rolled back before the block returned.

Fixes #36546

Great! Please add a thorough description to the PR.

I haven't spent a lot of time reviewing the change, but instead of the complicated manual corruption we can probably reproduce the same partial rollback is even simpler to reproduce with AssumeUTXO without corrupting or deleting files.

But given that I'm working on removing AssumeUTXO now, I think this remaining partial-state behavior should be documented as a known limitation instead of adding more AssumeUTXO-specific validation or regression code. 

<details>
<summary>Functional test reproducing the partial rollback</summary>

```diff
diff --git a/test/functional/feature_assumeutxo.py b/test/functional/feature_assumeutxo.py
index 8727a9925ec..250d31a4b09 100755
--- a/test/functional/feature_assumeutxo.py
+++ b/test/functional/feature_assumeutxo.py
@@ -660,6 +660,24 @@ class AssumeutxoTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
         self.assert_only_network_limited_service(n1)
         dumb_sync_blocks(src=n0, dst=n1, height=PAUSE_HEIGHT)
 
+        self.log.info("Test invalidateblock stops at the unavailable snapshot base")
+
+        def active_state():
+            info = n1.gettxoutsetinfo(use_index=False)
+            return {key: info[key] for key in ("bestblock", "hash_serialized_3")}
+
+        before = active_state()
+        snapshot_base = n1.getblockhash(SNAPSHOT_BASE_HEIGHT)
+        first_removed = n1.getblockhash(SNAPSHOT_BASE_HEIGHT + 1)
+        assert_equal(n1.invalidateblock(snapshot_base), None)  # TODO: should raise an RPC error
+        after = active_state()
+        assert_equal(after["bestblock"], snapshot_base)  # TODO: should be before["bestblock"]
+        assert_not_equal(after["hash_serialized_3"], before["hash_serialized_3"])  # TODO: should be unchanged
+
+        self.log.info("Restore the snapshot chain after the characterization")
+        n1.reconsiderblock(first_removed)
+        assert_equal(active_state(), before)
+
         self.log.info("Checking that blocks are segmented on disk")
         assert self.has_blockfile(n1, "00000"), "normal blockfile missing"
         assert self.has_blockfile(n1, "00001"), "assumed blockfile missing"
```
</details>

Please try to simplify the tests and maybe add the AssumeUTXO reproducer in a collapsible section in the PR (if you agree that it characterizes the same problem).
